intent_summary: The public Python API accepts series or canonical requests and returns the same numerical analysis used by the CLI and MCP compatibility interfaces.

criteria.criterion: analyze accepts bare ordered values with separate validated settings and dispatches canonical schema 1.0 or 1.1 requests.
criteria.notes: Bare values and separate settings validate before dispatch; canonical schema 1.0 and 1.1 requests use their respective contracts.

criteria.criterion: analyze_series preserves supplied settings and event-time context for a single dataset.
criteria.notes: Field-set handling preserves omitted versus explicit settings and context in the single-series wrapper, verified across dictionary and Settings inputs.

criteria.criterion: analyze_relationships preserves the declared multi-dataset relationship semantics.
criteria.notes: Declared relationships validate and use the shared engine without changing units, lineage, or primitive semantics.

criteria.criterion: Equivalent requests retain numerical results across Python, CLI, and full-result MCP compatibility calls apart from run IDs and runtime.
criteria.notes: Passing real CLI subprocess, Python, and full-result MCP parity tests compare stable numerical results apart from identity and runtime.
